request: At least 10 seconds made by actually combining multiple short clips, with continuity across the join as the focus.
plan: Reuse completed Kling4 A (~5.04s) and generate a new B (6s), then make a real direct cut. Expected edited duration around 11s; final must remain at least 10s.

b.input_role: Actual last frame of A as the exact first-frame target. No ending frame or third-party source video.
b.opening: Continue pedaling, rightward tracking, scale and camera height for 1.5s before any gentle camera rise.
b.middle: Follow the same connected trail around a shallow bend; change occlusion to reveal more existing bay.
b.ending: Continue riding and preserve the opened vista; no freeze or stop.

edit_policy.cut_candidate: A last-frame boundary, after comparing actual returned B opening and velocity
edit_policy.duplicate_reference_frame: Drop one duplicate boundary frame if actually repeated; do not hold the common pose twice.
edit_policy.speed: Original speed preferred; no looping, freezing or slowing clips to fake length.
edit_policy.transition: Direct cut so continuity is inspectable; do not use a dissolve to hide identity or geography changes.
edit_policy.normalization: Keep native originals; normalize delivery raster/fps only if required for the edit and record the transform.
edit_policy.audio: Check waveform/level continuity and record any technical smoothing. Do not claim listening if not performed.

acceptance: At least 10s actual edited video, with two independent AI clips and a documented cut
Rider identity, backpack and bicycle geometry persist across the cut
Pedal phase, tire position, forward speed and ground contact do not reset conspicuously
Camera direction, scale and parallax remain readable through the join
Trail, islands, arcades, waterfall and daylight remain geographically and visually coherent
Inspect at least 0.5s before and after the cut, and save a dedicated seam view
limits: A shared boundary image constrains appearance but does not guarantee inherited motion. The actual cut and duration depend on returned B; generation does not imply acceptance.
